summary: Server-side and shared utilities for the Next.js demo: a resilient HTTP/WebSocket client layer to the Barkpark API, a full advanced finder (dual-engine search, faceting, normalisation, live-search), and cross-surface glue between the content graph and finder results.

intentions.title: Eliminate per-request TLS overhead on the Vercel→Hetzner hop
intentions.evidence: bp-fetch.ts opens a persistent undici Agent (64 connections, 30s keep-alive) shared across all SSR requests; use-live-search.ts routes per-keystroke queries over a persistent Phoenix WebSocket to skip the Vercel hop entirely — both exist explicitly for latency, documented in their module headers

intentions.title: Provide a single resilient upstream abstraction (timeout, retry, structured errors)
intentions.evidence: bp-fetch.ts is the one place all server routes call the API: AbortController timeout, 2-retry backoff over the restart window, definitive-vs-transient error distinction, and defensive text→JSON parse; find-search.ts and graph.ts both import bpFetchJson and do no raw fetch themselves

intentions.title: Expose dual search engines (Postgres exact + Indx fuzzy) with transparent fallback
intentions.evidence: find.ts defines SearchEngine type and ENGINES metadata; find-search.ts selects the scoped Indx route only when a token is present and falls back to Postgres with an indxUnavailable flag; use-live-search.ts mirrors the same logic over the WebSocket path

intentions.title: Normalise heterogeneous document types into a uniform FindHit for the finder UI
intentions.evidence: find.ts normalizeHit derives title/excerpt/body/slug/date/facets from posts, papers, sheets, authors, categories — tolerating field aliases and PortableDoc block trees — so the finder renders any _type identically

intentions.title: Make the content graph and finder act as a single instrument (bidirectional hover + match highlighting)
intentions.evidence: hovered-doc-context.tsx provides two split contexts: graph-node hover publishes a doc-id that finder rows consume to highlight; finder result-set publishes weighted GraphMatch[] that the Canvas2D graph uses to dim unmatched nodes — two separate contexts to avoid cross-render churn

intentions.title: Keep private schemas out of browse/facet counts and keep both HTTP and WS paths consistent
intentions.evidence: find.ts DOC_TYPES allowlist (post/paper/sheet/page/author/category/project) is the single source; find-search.ts and use-live-search.ts both derive CONTENT_TYPES_CSV from it so neither can drift; omits siteSettings, navigation, etc.

intentions.title: Support multi-tenant scoped routes without breaking flat back-compat paths
intentions.evidence: barkpark-client.ts createClient() emits /w/<ws>/p/<project> paths when workspace+project are supplied and the flat /v1/... path otherwise; the exported `client` singleton uses the flat path for existing top-level routes

intentions.title: Surface content as a navigable knowledge graph on the landing
intentions.evidence: graph.ts fetches /v1/graph, normalises nodes/edges with field-alias tolerance, computes a rootId (highest-degree or 'barkpark' preferred), and caches the result for 5 min via unstable_cache tagged for webhook-driven revalidation; feeds the Canvas2D renderer

intentions.title: Record search events for anti-gaming correction auto-promotion
intentions.evidence: find-search.ts threads sessionId (from localStorage bp-search-client) as X-BP-SEARCH-CLIENT and sets X-BP-SEARCH-RECORD on non-browse queries; the returned searchEventId is carried through FindResponse for click attribution
